pointers.sentence: Each is a `django.db.models.Field` and a `CheckPostgresInstalledMixin`, whose check fails while `django.contrib.postgres` is not installed (`django/contrib/postgres/utils.py:CheckPostgresInstalledMixin`).

The lookups of these fields that write PostgreSQL's own operators are `PostgresOperatorLookup`s and write SQL in `as_postgresql` only: compiled for SQLite, `"crew__overlap"` raised `NotImplementedError` (`django/db/models/lookups.py:PostgresOperatorLookup.as_postgresql`).

`ArrayField` is given an instance of another field, `ArrayField.base_field`, and its column is that field's type with brackets after it: `"varchar(60)[]"` for the crew, `"varchar(60)[4]"` with `size=4` (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/array.py:ArrayField.db_type`).
PostgreSQL does not enforce the size, the documentation says (`docs/ref/contrib/postgres/fields.txt`): only Django checks it, by the `ArrayMaxLengthValidator` that `ArrayField.__init__` adds.

On the way in, `ArrayField.get_db_prep_value` and `ArrayField.get_db_prep_save` hand each item of a list to the base field's method of the same name, and the list goes to the driver as one parameter, which `ArrayField.get_placeholder_sql` casts to the column's type (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/array.py:ArrayField.get_placeholder_sql`).

An item `None` in an array of `django.db.models.JSONField` is saved as SQL NULL, not JSON null: `ArrayField.get_db_prep_save` hands it to `JSONField.get_db_prep_save`, which returns `None` as it is (`django/db/models/fields/json.py:JSONField.get_db_prep_save`).

`ArrayField.check` refuses a related field as the base, `"postgres.E002"`, and gathers the base field's errors but `"postgres.E005"` into one `"postgres.E001"` and its warnings into one `"postgres.W004"` (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/array.py:ArrayField.check`).

`ArrayField.check` refuses a related field as the base, `"postgres.E002"`, and gathers the base field's errors but `"postgres.E005"` into one `"postgres.E001"` and its warnings into one `"postgres.W004"` (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/array.py:ArrayField.check`). `ArrayField.validate` and `ArrayField.run_validators` run the base field's on each item and raise at the first that fails, its error rewritten by `prefix_validation_error` with the code `"item_invalid"` and the item's number: "Item 2 in the array did not validate: Ensure this value has at most 60 characters (it has 70)." (`django/contrib/postgres/utils.py:prefix_validation_error`). `ArrayField.validate` also refuses an array whose arrays differ in length.

`"contains"` (`"@>"`), `"contained_by"` (`"<@"`), `"overlap"` (`"&&"`) and `"exact"` on an array are built on `ArrayRHSMixin`, which turns a list on the right, unless it holds only `None`, into an `"ARRAY[...]"` of `Value`s prepared by the base field, and casts the right side to the column's type either way (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/array.py:ArrayRHSMixin`).
Any other name that is no lookup of the field goes to `ArrayField.get_transform` (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/array.py:ArrayField.get_transform`).

`django.contrib.postgres.fields.HStoreField` is a column of the type `"hstore"`, which a database has once the extension is created in it, by the migration operation `HStoreExtension` or by hand. `HStoreField.get_prep_value` makes each key a string and each value a string or `None`, so `{"salt": 40}` is saved as `{'salt': '40'}`; `HStoreField.validate`, which converts nothing, refuses it: "The value of “salt” is not a string or null." (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/hstore.py:HStoreField.validate`).

A name that is no lookup or transform of the field is a key: `HStoreField.get_transform` answers it with a `KeyTransformFactory`, whose transform writes `"->"` (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/hstore.py:HStoreField.get_transform`).

`RangeField` is the base of `IntegerRangeField` (`"int4range"`), `BigIntegerRangeField` (`"int8range"`), `DecimalRangeField` (`"numrange"`), `DateTimeRangeField` (`"tstzrange"`) and `DateRangeField` (`"daterange"`), each naming the model field of its bounds, `base_field`, a `range_type` and a form field (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/ranges.py`).
The range types are psycopg's, named in `django/db/backends/postgresql/psycopg_any.py`.

`RangeField.get_prep_value` makes a range of a list or tuple of two bounds (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/ranges.py:RangeField.get_prep_value`), with `ContinuousRangeField.default_bounds` on `DecimalRangeField` and `DateTimeRangeField`: `"[)"` unless the field was made with one of the other three (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/ranges.py:ContinuousRangeField.get_prep_value`).

`RangeField.get_prep_value` makes a range of a list or tuple of two bounds (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/ranges.py:RangeField.get_prep_value`), with `ContinuousRangeField.default_bounds` on `DecimalRangeField` and `DateTimeRangeField`: `"[)"` unless the field was made with one of the other three (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/ranges.py:ContinuousRangeField.get_prep_value`).

`"contains"` also takes one value, which `RangeContains` casts to the bounds' field; on the date and datetime ranges `"contains"` is `DateTimeRangeContains` instead, which casts it to the bounds' column type (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/ranges.py:DateTimeRangeContains.as_postgresql`).

`RangeContainedBy` asks the other question, a plain value in a range: importing the range fields' module registers it as `"contained_by"` on `models.DateField`, `models.DateTimeField`, `models.IntegerField`, `models.FloatField` and `models.DecimalField`, and it casts the range to the type `RangeContainedBy.type_mapping` gives the column (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/ranges.py:RangeContainedBy`).
`ArrayField.formfield` gives a `SimpleArrayField` of the base field's form field, the size its maximum (`django/contrib/postgres/forms/array.py:SimpleArrayField`).

`BaseRangeField.compress` refuses a start after the end and makes the range with the bounds `ContinuousRangeField.formfield` passed it, if any (`django/contrib/postgres/forms/ranges.py:BaseRangeField.compress`).

`django/contrib/postgres/validators.py` has validators of a list's length (`ArrayMaxLengthValidator`, `ArrayMinLengthValidator`), an hstore's keys (`KeysValidator`) and a range's bounds (`RangeMaxValueValidator`, `RangeMinValueValidator`, for which a missing bound is beyond any limit).
`CICharField`, `CIEmailField` and `CITextField` remain only so that old migrations import (`django/contrib/postgres/fields/citext.py`).
